reason: The sources provide sufficient details to support a short, engaging summary of the Gemini 8 emergency.
story: In March 1966, Neil Armstrong and David Scott achieved the world's first space docking during the Gemini 8 mission. Shortly after connecting with an Agena target vehicle, a terrifying malfunction occurred. A thruster short-circuited and stuck open, sending the combined spacecraft into a violent, uncontrolled spin that reached nearly a revolution per second. Believing the target vehicle was at fault, Armstrong undocked, but the separation only accelerated Gemini 8's rotation. Threatened with blacking out, Armstrong shut down the orbital thrusters and fired the reentry control system, using 75 percent of their emergency fuel to stabilize the ship. The harrowing near-miss forced an immediate mission abort, a splashdown in the Pacific, and a complete redesign of NASA spacecraft electrical systems.
angle: When Neil Armstrong undocked from their target vehicle to escape a violent spin, his capsule spun even faster, nearly causing him and David Scott to black out.

claims.claim: The mission successfully completed the first U.S. space docking.
Astronauts Neil Armstrong and David Scott crewed the Gemini 8 mission.
A stuck thruster caused the spacecraft to go into a violent spin.
Armstrong undocked from the Agena, but Gemini's rotation accelerated further.
The spin rate reached up to 296 degrees per second or nearly one revolution per second.
Armstrong activated the Reentry Control System (RCS) after shutting down the OAMS.
The emergency stabilization maneuver used 75 percent of their reentry control fuel.
Mission rules required an immediate abort once the RCS was fired.
The crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean and was picked up by the USS Leonard F. Mason.
Investigation concluded that OAMS thruster number 8 had short-circuited.
Subsequent spacecraft designs were modified so individual thrusters had isolated circuits.

disputed: The exact landing location coordinates and distance east of Okinawa vary slightly between sources (e.g., 800 km versus 600 miles), which can be generalized as an emergency splashdown east of Okinawa.
